feedback: Before this robot races, the evidence from iteration 0 is clear. All 60 trials (oval, s-bend, slalom) went off track with 0 completions. Progress was 0.09 to 0.21, with about one line-loss event per run, and max_error was about 0.063 m, just above the 0.06 m off-track limit. Body width cannot relax that limit (max(0.06, 0.0125 + bw/4) stays at 0.06 for bw up to 0.18), so sensing is the lever. What I had to compensate for in the controller: with the ±0.04 m row the weights had to be scaled to about 50 per metre, and the signal could jump when an outer sensor reached the tape. For the wider ±0.06 m row I rescaled the weights to about 33 per metre and raised kp to 6.0 to keep the steering gain, and I raised kd slightly to damp the lighter body. Please keep the sensor row's forward offset at y = 0.03 m unless the next race shows the robot reacting too late. Next race guidance: if the wider ±0.06 m span still gives line_loss_events of 1 or more on the slalom or s-bend, with max_error still near 0.06 m, widen the span to ±0.08 m, the largest allowed sensor x. If line losses are gone but max_error still exceeds 0.06 m on the oval, the issue is tracking lag rather than sensing, so move the row forward to y = 0.05 m. If steering_oscillation rises markedly with the larger 16 mm footprint, reduce sensor_size to 0.012 m.
requested_changes: If the next race still shows line_loss_events of 1 or more with max_error near 0.06 m on the slalom or s-bend, widen the sensor span to x = ±0.08 (for example -0.08, -0.04, 0.0, 0.04, 0.08 or seven sensors at ±0.08 spacing); this is based on iteration 0, where the ±0.04 m row lost the tape at about 0.05 m and every run went off track.

If line losses are gone but max_error still exceeds 0.06 m on the oval, move the sensor row forward to y = 0.05 m to give the controller more lead; iteration 0 showed the drift starts after the line is lost, so the lead matters.

If the 16 mm footprint produces higher steering_oscillation than iteration 0 (which was 0.14 to 0.16), try sensor_size 0.012 m to reduce the centre noise, since the 0.012 m footprint gave a clean graded signal in iteration 0.
